newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite Senate President Margaret Reid saying she hoped Senator Mal Colston would resign as deputy president, Colston yesterday issued a statement through a spokesman for Brisbane's Wesley Hospital which discussed his health rather than his political future. Page 3.

Participants in the New South Wales and Victorian wholesale electricity markets are understood to have agreed to issue a statement announcing an April 27 start-up date for the initial stage of the national electricity market. The first phase will establish an interstate wholesale electricity grid by linking the two State markets. Page 3.

In a landmark dispute that may affect the direction of pay outcomes throughout the metals industry, industry unions have launched a campaign of industrial action at the five Melbourne plants of Email Group, which is offering wage rises of between 2 per cent and 4 per cent a year - a fraction of the unions' demand for 15 per cent over two years. Page 3.

Federal Government efforts to resolve the controversial Wik issue this week have been hindered with the mining industry now arguing that Aborigines who prove native title rights over a pastoral lease should retain a "right to negotiate", arguing that the Federal Government's plan to remove this right could amount to the extinguishment of native title on farms. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which is widely seen in legal circles as one of defiance, Australia's chief justices will today release the first Declaration of Principles on Judicial Independence in the wake of concerted attacks from the Federal Government. The declaration stesses judicial impartiality and reinforces the importance of public confidence in the judiciary. Page 1.

Pressure mounted on Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday after only three of more than 200 delegates at the Queensland National Party central council meeting stood up to applaud him while Qld Premier Rob Borbidge threatened to cut links with Prime Minister John Howard if he did not get an acceptable resolution on native title. Page 1.

The Federal Opposition has called on the Coalition to not be intimidated by the prospect of Iranian trade bans after it was announced in the Iranian Parliament yesterday that a planned visit to Iran next month by a delegation from the Australia-Iran Chamber of Commerce and Industry would be cancelled following the Federal Government's recalling of its ambassador. Australia's move came amid allegations the Iranian Government was involved in international terrorism. Page 1.

Speaking after the release of a survey of Melbourne medical practitioners which revealed that 22 admitted they assisted terminally ill patients to die, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said it was futile having laws that were "openly defied" and called for voluntary euthanasia to be legalised. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite claims from Senate President Margaret Reid yesterday that the Senate may have been seriously misled in the Colston scandal, the Federal Government is resisting pressure for a Senate inquiry into claims that the embattled Independent Senator conspied with a staff member to fabricate an explanation for his over-claiming of travel allowances. Page 1.

Australia's eight chief justices of the States and Territories, including the Chief Justice of New South Wales, Justice Gleeson, last night issued an unprecedented statement, titled A Declaration of Principles of Judicial Independence, which set down their own principles for the appointment of judges, describing as objectionable the use of acting judges to avoid permanent appointments to the Bench. Page 1.

According to documents obtained under the Freedom of Information Act, the Howard Government was forced by the departments of Prime Minister and Cabinet and Foreign Affairs and Trade, together with AusAID, to spend A$55 million on a massive bridge in Vietnm instead of expanding humanitarian programs in health, education and landmine clearance. Page 3.

As the smallgoods industry announced an A$800,000 review of 1,400 "backyard" meat processors, Aussie Beef Thin and Aussie Beef Thick sausages made by Woolworths smallgoods division, Chisholm Manufacturing, were recalled on Saturday after brittle metal framents were found in the products. The in-house recall is the company's third in a week. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a move which would reverse a Federal Government election commitment not to downgrade Radio Australia, Communications Minister Richard Alston will take a submission to Cabinet tomorrow that would reduce Radio Australia to an English-only service, just a the station nears completion of a A$15 million capital works program. Page 1.

In a move which is widely seen as part of a strategy to reinforce Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's grip over the ruling party, he has forced the resignation of Muhammad Muhammad Taib, one of the richest and most influential figures in Malaysian politics, who is fighting charges of trying to illegally export A$1.2 million in cash from Australia. Page 1.

Debra Conomy, a witness in the Operation Bart internal police corruption probe who gave information on alleged kickbacks to police from window-shutter operators, says she and her family have been harassed and victimised by police as payback for helping inestigators. Page 1.

After being admitted to hospital on Thursday after suffering effects of the flu, embattled Senator Mal Colston announced yesterday he would make no decisions about his political future while he was ill, defying pressure to stand down as Deputy Senate Presdent as police today begin investigations concerning his alleged parliamentary travel rorts. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
